name: Inonotus obliquus

size_cm.note: general knowledge, unchecked (research/08); the sterile black canker; the true fruit body is a hidden crust

notes: A trunk heart rot that grows for decades in the living tree and fruits once, after the tree dies. What is seen is a sterile black canker, not the fruit body.

tip_speed.note: Claude's inference from the species' ecology and general knowledge, not from a measurement (2026-11-10): slow heart-rot of living birch that takes years to form a conk; set below the family default

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found
